title: Canada Study Permit Wait Times Rise as Work Permits Hit 2026 Low
excerpt: IRCC's latest processing data shows a split picture: in-Canada work permits reached their fastest level this year at 122 days, while study permit waits for Indian applicants climbed to five weeks.
body:
• In-Canada work permit processing times fell to 122 days as of July 22 — the fastest pace recorded in 2026, approaching IRCC's 120-day service standard.
  • Study permit wait times for Indian applicants rose to five weeks, up from three weeks in April, and in-Canada study permit processing climbed to seven weeks.
  • Pakistan saw the sharpest work permit increase, jumping from seven to 10 weeks in a single reporting cycle.
  • Study permit times have held steady for four consecutive weeks across most countries after the earlier increases.

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada published its latest processing time data on July 22, revealing a split picture for temporary residence applicants: work permits continued their months-long improvement trend while study permit wait times remained elevated after climbing earlier this summer.

The data, which IRCC updates weekly based on how long 80 percent of recently completed applications took to process, is the primary planning tool for hundreds of thousands of applicants from India, the largest source country for both Canadian study and work permits.

Work Permits Approach Target

In-Canada work permit processing fell to 122 days, down from 124 days a week earlier and 129 days at the start of July. The current figure is now just two days above IRCC's service standard of 120 days — a sharp turnaround from the 255-day processing times recorded in March.

For Indian applicants outside Canada, work permit waits remained steady at nine weeks. The United States held at three weeks, and Nigeria at six weeks.

Pakistan was the outlier. Work permit processing times there jumped from seven to 10 weeks — a three-week increase in a single reporting cycle. The Philippines also ticked up, from six to seven weeks. IRCC has not publicly explained the cause of these increases, though shifts in application volumes and complexity of cases are common factors.

Study Permits Tell a Different Story

Study permit processing times have been a source of frustration since early summer. Indian applicants now face a five-week wait, up from the three-week low recorded in April. In-Canada study permit processing sits at seven weeks, up from six weeks at the start of June.

The current figures have stabilized — study permit wait times remained unchanged across all tracked countries for four consecutive weeks through July 22. But for students targeting September 2026 intakes, the earlier increases have compressed planning timelines.

Processing times by country as of July 22:

  • Inside Canada: 7 weeks
  • India: 5 weeks
  • Pakistan: 6 weeks
  • Nigeria: 5 weeks
  • United States: 5 weeks
  • Philippines: 4 weeks

The Broader Context

The mixed results reflect competing pressures on Canada's immigration system. The federal government has been working to clear backlogs accumulated during the pandemic and the surge of applications that followed, particularly in the temporary residence category. In-Canada work permits, which were taking over 250 days to process as recently as March, have seen the most dramatic improvement — a reduction of more than 130 days in four months.

At the same time, Canada has been tightening controls on temporary immigration. Study permit caps introduced in 2024 reduced the number of new permits issued, and the government has continued to adjust intake targets amid political pressure over housing costs and public services.

For Indian applicants, who make up the single largest group of Canadian study and work permit holders, the data presents a planning challenge. Those applying for work permits face improving timelines, while students may need to account for processing periods roughly double what they were in spring.

What to Watch

IRCC's next weekly update was expected around July 29. The monthly permanent residence processing time refresh, last updated July 7, showed the Canadian Experience Class holding at six months and non-Express Entry Provincial Nominee Programs dropping to 12 months. Citizenship certificate processing, however, has ballooned to 19 months — the third consecutive monthly increase after sitting at just three months in March.
nri_angle: Indian students and workers applying for Canadian permits face divergent timelines — faster work permits but slower study permits, complicating planning for fall 2026 intakes.
